raw_answer_text:
A1: The switch learns from the source address of every frame it receives, regardless of whether the destination address is found or the forwarding outcome.
A2: It associates the source MAC address with the port on which the frame arrived.
A3: Whether the destination MAC address of the frame is found in the switch's address table (and mapped to a specific port).
A4: The switch floods the frame out all ports except the port on which it was received.
A5: Both are flooded out all ports (except the incoming port); a switch treats an unknown-unicast destination the same way it treats broadcast/multicast frames.
A6: When the destination address is in the table and maps to the same port on which the frame arrived (source and destination are on the same segment).
A7: Frames are no longer flooded; instead they are forwarded only out the single port learned for that destination.
A8: Both ports must be in the forwarding (learning/forwarding) state, i.e., not blocked or disabled.
